what: CAL-P1077 / CERT-2428 — how exposed each cell is to the id-range rail's re-derivation defect. A virtual question whose markets all fall inside one of sweep()'s [lo + kW, lo + (k+1)W) slices cannot be re-derived by that rail; one that straddles a boundary can. This is the EXPOSURE, not the damage - and the two do not track each other, which is the finding.
method: TWO bases, and the cheap one is validated against the exact one. EXACT: read off a frozen whole-vm Stage A roster, so the unit is the producer's own vm_id. PROXY: futures_markets.group_id via one db-query, over the RAW cell (no eligibility filter, no >=3 gate), so its straddling count is an UPPER BOUND on the exact one - measured as 137 >= 112 on economics and 466 >= 465 on hockey. Its percentage is NOT comparable to the exact one because the denominators differ (7,437 raw groups vs 1,181 gated virtual questions on economics); use the COUNT. The bound is one-directional and that is the point: PROXY 0 => EXACT 0, conclusively, because a group whose ids never cross a boundary cannot be split by one however it is grouped or gated - so a zero row is a finished answer, and a non-zero row is only a reason to fold on the whole-vm rail.

kalshi/golf.basis: futures_markets.group_id via db-query (upper bound, no roster frozen)
kalshi/golf.note: ZERO. Every kalshi/golf group's markets fall inside a single slice, so the id-range rail cannot re-derive any golf question's identity and its arm table is not exposed to the CERT-2428 defect.

triage_reading: kalshi/golf, kalshi/entertainment and kalshi/tech are at ZERO: the id-range rail cannot re-derive any question identity in those cells, so a fold already taken there needs no refold. polymarket/golf (<=1), cricket (<=55), economics (<=137) and hockey (<=466) are exposed and must be folded on the whole-vm rail - which economics and hockey now have been, both agreeing with the id-range rail anyway. Exposure bounds the risk; it does not predict the damage.
